scope: Independent PRE_DEPLOY review of the exact SQL migration/recovery candidate and guarded activation script. This is not evidence of production application, credited accounts, a live cron run, frontend publication or Git push.

baselineVerification.source: Read-only production metadata captured by parent in .tmp/savings-auto-contributions/functions.json, private-functions.json and tables.json; reviewer made no production request.
baselineVerification.method: Independently parsed the SQL embedded baseline arrays and compared every function hash/owner/ACL and complete table metadata with captured source. Inspected diffs of replaced readers, receipt core and the private operation writer.
baselineVerification.result: Exact baseline guards agree; protected original financial logic remains except the declared shared receipt extraction, first positive contribution anchor and pending-receipt barrier on total settlement.

verifiedDesign.subject: Money, identity and corrections
verifiedDesign.result: Public manual capability/signature preserved; private shared core retains exact active identity, certification cutoff, finalized yield decisions, receipt version, existing ledger agreement and held-capital guards. Actual zero remains authoritative. A later correction posts only the delta. Zero followed by a positive receipt obtains a real CONTRIBUTION anchor in the original semester.

verifiedDesign.subject: Future instructions and plan changes
verifiedDesign.result: Instructions are private, versioned and nonmonetary until due. The selected plan must still cover the date and remain unique/canonical. The semantic hash protects amount/process/identity/start/source without invalidating an earlier covered date merely because the plan later ends. Changed or overlapping plans produce review, never substituted money.

verifiedDesign.subject: Idempotency, calendar and scheduler
verifiedDesign.result: Private cron uses the existing Hermosillo calendar, an explicit activation floor and deterministic enrollment/date key. Existing receipts always win. Any previous ledger evidence without a receipt, including a reversed net-zero amount, blocks automatic creation. The worker serializes job/config/identity/enrollment, retains failed attempts and reports remaining work instead of a false complete result.

verifiedDesign.subject: Total withdrawal and pause
verifiedDesign.result: The existing participant/enrollment lock protects a read-only pending-receipt barrier before total settlement. It does not create money or invert the config lock. A pause does not erase previously authorized due obligations. Initial never-activated policy preserves prior behavior. Existing fixed request amount, availability, loan attestation and period allocation checks remain; a stale total is not increased implicitly.

verifiedDesign.subject: Security and provenance
verifiedDesign.result: New tables force RLS with no client/service grants. Private worker/core are not browser capabilities. New public RPCs require existing savings.config or savings.write permissions. Empty search_path, source/actor CHECK and null-safe idempotency prevent impersonating a human actor. Existing table/service boundaries are retained.

verifiedDesign.subject: Recovery
verifiedDesign.result: Both phases acquire job then config locks. Recovery unschedules only this job and pauses it. Any receipt, instruction, run or policy history prevents structural deletion; failed-only history is preserved too. A clean unused installation can restore exact definitions/ACL/owners under drift checks. No monetary deletion or broad reversal is attempted.

resolvedFindings: Ambiguous overlapping plans must not be selected silently by the automatic writer.
A previous ledger with net zero must not be treated as a blank date and credited again.
Recovery must preserve failed runs and serialize both phases against workers and instructions.
Paused automation must not let a total withdrawal hide already authorized pending contributions.
Limited batches must expose remaining work; an existing cron name must not be overwritten.
An instruction valid for an earlier date must survive an ordinary later plan closure.
Release checks for exact counts, per-account changes, untouched history, unrelated enrollment dates and actor provenance belong before COMMIT and must fail closed on NULL.

independentCommands: Read-only comparison of embedded migration guards against captured live metadata: PASS, 13 functions and 13 tables.
Read-only function diff inspection against public and private snapshots: PASS within declared scope.
verification.testAssessment: Reviewed isolated test implementation and the recorded PASS evidence; checked its exact hashes independently. Tests exercise real candidate SQL with isolated schema/functions. This reviewer did not rerun the SQL suite or execute the release script.
verification.concurrencyAssessment: Inspected lock order and sequential manual-before-worker/worker-before-correction outcomes. Simultaneous PostgreSQL sessions were not exercised; no live concurrency claim is made.

releaseScriptReview.result: Candidate evidence/hash binding, installed metadata revalidation, job-before-config locks, exact authorized due set, 294 receipt/transaction counts and policy audit count, delta per affected account, protected historical rows and enrollment dates, NULL-safe ledger/audit validation are checked before committing. A second run is required to create no financial change. Secrets and row backups remain private.
releaseScriptReview.limits: Inspection of the stated hash only. Its future readback additions and any subsequent delta must be verified by the release owner. The script is a guarded execution plan, not proof that activation has occurred.

limits: Auth, pg_cron transport and payout attestation are simulated in the isolated SQL suite; existing underlying permission/loan guards were preserved by source inspection.
Real scheduled execution, production permission/readback, authorized exact account deltas, zero-change repeated run, frontend behavior and publication remain release gates.
No reviewer production login, SQL operation, Google request or financial write occurred. Only this review JSON was added.
No approval is given to a different migration/recovery hash or to synthetic financial testing in production.
